subject.title: feat(channels): core-owned durable ingress drain — one turn-adoption lifecycle, Telegram first

question: Should OpenClaw permanently publish this narrowed durable-ingress drain and turn-adoption lifecycle through the plugin runtime and `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-outbound`?
rationale: The implementation is well-proven, but choosing a permanent plugin API and its compatibility obligations requires maintainer intent that contributor comments and automated review cannot establish.

options.title: Approve the narrow seam
options.body: Accept the current factory, lifecycle binding, types, constants, and restricted runtime method as the permanent extension contract, then land after refreshed gates.

options.title: Keep the drain internal
options.body: Remove the public runtime and SDK exposure and use a bundled-only internal bridge, reducing external compatibility obligations but postponing reuse by external channel plugins.

options.title: Defer the public contract
options.body: Land only the core engine and Telegram migration through a temporary internal boundary, then review the SDK surface separately once another channel consumer is ready.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow seam
recommendation.body: Accept the current factory, lifecycle binding, types, constants, and restricted runtime method as the permanent extension contract, then land after refreshed gates.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged plugin SDK narrowing and channel-runtime refactors provide the clearest available ownership signal for this API-surface choice.
